threads.body: Same concern as in the shared stream wrapper: catching `BaseException` here will record `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` as failures. If the intent is specifically to capture cancellation (`asyncio.CancelledError`), consider excluding process-terminating exceptions from the `fail()` path (and apply the same pattern to the other instrumentation wrappers changed in this PR).

threads.body: Catching `BaseException` will also intercept `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, and `GeneratorExit`, which are typically not desirable to treat as invocation failures (even if re-raised). Consider either (a) explicitly excluding those types (re-raise without calling `_finalize_failure`) or (b) switching to a two-branch approach that handles cancellation explicitly while keeping `Exception` for the rest.

+def test_wrapped_call_base_exception_is_recorded_and_reraised(
+    handler, span_exporter
+):
+    def wrapped(*_args, **_kwargs):
+        raise asyncio.CancelledError()
+
+    traced = embeddings_create(handler)
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        traced(wrapped, _make_client(), (), {"model": "m"})
+
+    spans = span_exporter.get_finished_spans()
+    assert len(spans) == 1
+    span = spans[0]
+    assert span.attributes["error.type"] == "asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError"
